Maintenance Report — MNT-0038-001

Asset: WELL-0038 (SW-23 Well 038, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 11 Nov 2022 08:00 · Finished: 11 Nov 2022 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0038-0004 on 2022-11-10 Report written: 12 Nov 2022

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0038-0004 at 15:00 on 2022-11-10 found crude oil on the pad: about 1.4% of the pad area, estimated 0.8 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 318 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 254 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0038-001 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.82% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0038-009

Asset: WELL-0038 (SW-23 Well 038, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 17 Nov 2023 08:00 · Finished: 22 Nov 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 114 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0038-0057 on 2023-11-16 Report written: 23 Nov 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0038-0057 showed the wellhead at 18.3 °C with the air at 17.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0038-011

Asset: WELL-0038 (SW-23 Well 038, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 06 Jan 2024 08:00 · Finished: 10 Jan 2024 17:00 · Well stopped for this job: 105 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0038-0064 on 2024-01-04 Report written: 10 Jan 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0038-0064 showed the wellhead at 21.2 °C with the air at 12.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 2 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Review sand control on this well.
  • Send the old pump for teardown.

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0038-0156 showed the wellhead at 18.1 °C with the air at 17.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.
